A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same two-stage entropy-guided GRPO study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material that was relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and evaluation results for GUI grounding, fine-grained classification, and open-vocabulary object detection, together with ablations and out-of-distribution evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds model, benchmark, preprocessing, and text-reasoning experiments, including results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The two-stage entropy strategy and Algorithm 1 are retained, but the specified GRPO loss changes: Eqs. (2)–(3) acquire negative signs, and Eq. (3) revises response aggregation. This is a limited correction to the documented optimization objective; the PDFs do not establish that the training implementation changed.

E1.justification: V2 adds OS-World-G evaluation, MMBench-GUI L2 evaluation and training, and GSM8K text-based mathematical reasoning. These substantially broaden the evaluated environments and tasks. ScreenSpot, Pets37, ScreenSpot-Pro, and COCO detection were already present in v1; relocating the detection experiment does not add coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain the base model, standard GRPO, entropy minimization, entropy maximization, and the retained Figure 1 reward baselines. New benchmarks largely reuse these comparators. Coordinate-format and resizing variants are preprocessing controls rather than new competing methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds InternVL-3.5-2B and Qwen2.5-3B configurations, four-rollout preprocessing controls, and MMBench-GUI training with 500 training/test samples each, switching at step 400 and evaluating at step 500. ScreenSpot-Pro sampling changes in the description from 150 total samples to 150 per category. Its retained scores do not establish that evaluation was rerun under that revised setting.

E4.justification: V2 adds absolute-versus-relative coordinate and image-resizing robustness tests under fully noisy supervision, expands OOD analyses, and introduces MMBench-GUI in-domain experiments explicitly motivated by contamination concerns. Model-family analysis also extends to InternVL. The original switching-point, stage-order, and noisy-data-scaling ablations remain.

E5.justification: Figure 3(b) adds shaded bands around training-accuracy curves; v1 shows only lines in that panel. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 does not define the new bands. Thus the visual uncertainty reporting changes without establishing additional runs or a particular statistical estimator.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results, including MMBench-GUI OOD accuracy of 60.6% versus 57.0% for GRPO on clean training data, but GSM8K clean-data accuracy of 79.6% versus GRPO's 81.4%. Existing Table 1 values remain unchanged. Table 2 corrects Qwen2.5-VL-3B GRPO at 50% noise from 76.0% to 76.2%, and Figure 3(b) changes the plotted accuracy trajectories.

T1.justification: Eqs. (2)–(3) correct the GRPO loss/gradient signs, replace response-index averaging with an explicit group sum, and introduce response-specific lengths. These are limited mathematical revisions. The entropy definitions and piecewise schedule remain, and no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central exploration-then-exploitation contribution remains. V1's claims of consistently outperforming alternatives across the board are qualified in v2 as superior overall robustness and superiority in most noise settings. The contribution statement also shifts emphasis from partially labeled or unlabeled learning toward noisy supervision.

C2.justification: V2 extends the prior-ability limitation to Qwen2-VL-2B, explains that unknown label correctness favors a unified schedule over subset-specific assignments, and interprets preprocessing controls as supporting intrinsic GRPO noise tolerance. It also introduces a contamination-based rationale for MMBench-GUI evaluation. The main exploration/exploitation explanation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code repository address, the InternVL training framework, KL coefficients of 0.04 for GUI grounding and zero for classification, and further benchmark implementation details. Appendix B states that detection shares classification settings. These are additional disclosures; the original hardware, training-time estimates, and most hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds eight references covering new datasets, model families, and related RLVR work. Section 2.2 reframes annotation-free learning around noisy annotations and revises how external and internal reward sources are characterized. The principal external-signal, internal-signal, and entropy-based positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology explanations, and experimental discussion undergo extensive editing. Discussions move inside the experiments section, model comparisons move into main results, and limitations move to a reorganized, lettered appendix. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 5 expand, a new main-text OOD table and several appendix tables appear, and Algorithm 1 moves to the supplement. Figure 3 is redrawn with revised labels, legends, and shaded accuracy bands; Figures 1–2 also receive labeling changes. Existing detection and ablation tables are retained with revised placement and formatting.

improvement.justification: The broader evaluations and preprocessing controls make the empirical evidence more informative, including revealing failures on new tasks. Corrected equations, several corrected numerical summaries, and added implementation information improve assessability. However, the ScreenSpot-Pro sample-size revision remains unreconciled, Figure 3's new bands are undefined, and the new OOD superiority discussion overstates Table 5. These shortcomings limit the overall benefit despite the substantial expansion.
